summary: This bill eliminates federal income tax on Social Security benefits by terminating IRC Section 86 after enactment and appropriating Treasury funds to offset resulting shortfalls in Social Security trust funds.

scores.thoughts: The bill appropriates Treasury funds to hold Social Security trust funds harmless from lost tax revenue transfers. This requires new outlays from general revenue, expanding government spending to offset the change.
The core provision repeals Section 86, eliminating federal income tax on Social Security benefits. This is a direct, broad-based tax reduction for recipients.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, Medicare structure, or related regulations.

Making Social Security benefits tax-free increases recipients' net income, effectively expanding benefits under a major safety-net program.

The tax repeal reduces revenue while the hold-harmless clause increases outlays; the bill explicitly rejects tax increases to offset costs, increasing deficits and debt.
